Chapter 2: The Franks and the Office—Building Trust in Uncertain Times.
Picture this: right in the heart of Amsterdam, there’s a small office. On the surface, it’s just a workplace—papers shuffled, phones ringing, and the air filled with the scent of spices wafting in from the warehouse below. But it’s more than that. It’s where a handful of lives, about to be forever changed, start to intertwine.
The man running the place is quiet, but there’s a calm determination in how he goes about things. He treats his staff with genuine warmth and respect, never missing a chance for a kind word. His family, fresh from Germany and hoping for a new beginning, brings a sense of hope to the office—even as uncertainty grows outside.
One of the women working alongside him can’t help but notice the subtle ways he tries to shield his loved ones from the dangers creeping closer. His wife, soft-spoken and gentle, sometimes drops by with their two daughters. The younger girl is a burst of energy—curious, always laughing. Her older sister, though, hangs back, taking in the world with a cautious gaze.
As weeks turn into months, the city’s mood shifts. Suddenly, new restrictions are everywhere—Jews can’t go to parks, schools, or even certain shops. But inside the office, for a few precious hours each day, life almost feels normal. The staff—each with their own background and beliefs—find themselves leaning on each other. A shared joke here, an extra sandwich there. Little moments of kindness that mean everything.
And that’s where trust really starts to grow. The manager opens up to the woman, confiding his fears about the future and his fierce need to protect his family. She listens, tries her best to reassure him, but the truth is, she feels the weight too. It’s one thing to care for friends when times are tough. It’s another to realize their safety might one day depend on your choices.
The office becomes more than just a place to work—it’s a lifeline. People bring in extra food to share, trade news about their families, and quietly help each other find a way through the maze of new rules. The bonds that form in those cramped rooms are about to be tested in ways none of them could possibly imagine.
Then, the moment comes when the family has to disappear—to step out of sight and into hiding. It’s not a decision anyone takes lightly. It’s a leap into the unknown, driven by desperation, but also by trust. The woman and her husband agree to help, understanding the risks but knowing they can’t just stand by. That ordinary office, once filled with routines and everyday chatter, is about to become a secret refuge—a hiding place built on kindness, courage, and the trust they’ve built together.
